{{nihongo|'''Miho Shrine'''|御穂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Suruga Province]].

``Miho Shrine'' is located in {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}{{ill|Shizuoka (city)|Q174691|qid=Q174691}}{{ill|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|ar|شيميزو كو|ceb|Shimizu-ku|es|Shimizu-ku (Shizuoka)|fa|شیمیزو-کو، شیزوئوکا|fr|Shimizu-ku|id|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|it|Shimizu-ku|ja|清水区|ko|시미즈구|simple|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|tr|Shimizu, Şizuoka (semt)|uk|Район Сімідзу|ur|شیمیزو وارڈ، شیزوکا|vi|Shimizu (quận)|war|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|zh|清水區 (日本)|qid=Q79385}} Miho. {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, {{ill|Suruga Province|ckb|پارێزگای سروگا|cs|Provincie Suruga|de|Provinz Suruga|eo|Provinco Suruga|es|Provincia de Suruga|fa|ولایت سوروگا|fr|Province de Suruga|gl|Provincia de Suruga|hak|Suruga-koet|id|Provinsi Suruga|it|Suruga (provincia)|ja|駿河国|ko|스루가국|lt|Surugos žemė|nl|Suruga (provincie)|pt|Província de Suruga|ru|Суруга (провинция)|simple|Suruga Province|sk|Suruga (provincia)|sr|Провинција Суруга|th|แคว้นซูรูงะ|tr|Suruga (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Суруґа|vi|Tỉnh Suruga|zh|駿河國|zh_min_nan|Suruga-kok|zh_yue|駿河國|qid=Q864170}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}, {{ill|Q712534|lt=old company rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=prefectural company}}.It is known as a shrine related to ``Hagoromo no Matsu'' in {{ill|Miho no Matsubara|Q869275|qid=Q869275|lt=Miho no Matsubara}}. The character ``Miho'' is also used for ``Miho'', ``Miho'', and ``Miho'' {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}}.

The shrine precincts and the approach (the path of the gods) are {{ill|Cultural heritage|Q210272|qid=Q210272|lt=World Cultural Heritage}} <ref> [http://www.shizuoka-citypromotion.jp/mihonomatsubara/learn/area.html Constituent assets Miho no Matsubara Range] (Shizuoka City). </ref>.

The following two deities are enshrined. </ref>.

:* '''{{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫|zh|三穗津姬|qid=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime no Mikoto}}''' (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto)
In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmeicho}}, there is one deity enshrined. Also, in "Suruga Zoshi", the two pillars are "Miho Tsuhiko" and "Miho Tsuhime" {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
[[File:Port of Shimizu and Miho Coast Areas Aerial photograph.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|Aerial photograph around the Miho Peninsula}}{{Small|Composite of 12 photos taken in 1983. {{National Aerial Photography}}. The corner to the right of the center of the image is the precincts of Miho Shrine, and a row of pine trees extends from the precincts to {{ill|Miho no Matsubara|Q869275|qid=Q869275}} on the coast. }}]]
Founding date is unknown. In "Suruga Zoshi", it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nippon Takeru}} donated government money and shrine territory by imperial order to Mihosaki, Izumo Province (currently {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|qid=Q132751}}{{ill|Matsue|ar|ماتسوا (شيمانه)|arz|ماتسوا|az|Matsue|azb|ماتسوئه|ban|Matsué, Shimané|bar|Matsue|bg|Мацуе|ca|Matsue|ce|Мацуэ|ceb|Matsue Shi|cs|Macue|da|Matsue|de|Matsue|eo|Macuo|es|Matsue (Shimane)|et|Matsue|eu|Matsue|fa|ماتسوئه|fi|Matsue|fr|Matsue|ga|Matsue|gl|Matsue|hak|Matsue-sṳ|hu|Macue|hy|Մացուե|id|Matsue, Shimane|it|Matsue|ja|松江市|ko|마쓰에시|lt|Macujė|mg|Matsue|mzn|ماتسوئه|nl|Matsue|no|Matsue (Shimane)|pl|Matsue|pt|Matsue|ro|Matsue|ru|Мацуэ|sc|Matsue|sh|Matsue|simple|Matsue|sr|Мацуе|sv|Matsue|sw|Matsue, Shimane|tg|Матсуе|th|มัตสึเอะ|tl|Matsue|tr|Matsue|tt|Матсуе|tum|Matsue|uk|Мацуе|ur|ماتسو، شیمانے|vi|Matsue|war|Matsue, Shimane|wuu|松江市|zh|松江市|zh_classical|松江市|zh_min_nan|Matue-chhī|zh_yue|松江市|qid=Q207321}}It is also said that the deity was relocated from Mihonoseki Town), but it is not clear {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.{{ill|Miho no Matsubara|Q869275|qid=Q869275|lt=Miho no Matsubara}} has the ``Hagoromo no Matsu'', and from Hagoromo no Matsu to the head of Miho Shrine there is a line of pine trees, but this tree-lined road is It is said to be the path for the gods who descended from the pine trees to reach Miho Shrine, and is called the ``Kami no Michi'' {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}. Even today, during the Tsutsugayu Shinto ritual, a ceremony is held on the shore to welcome the gods, and at that time, the Himorogi that the gods rely on are brought into the precincts through a row of pine trees.{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}. From these, the rituals at Miho Shrine are thought to be part of the ``Eternal Faith'' that welcomes the gods from the ``{{ill|Tokoyo no kuni|Q11060259|qid=Q11060259|lt=Eternal Country}}'' beyond the sea.{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}.

=== Outline ===
In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokukushi}}, the name of the god is ``Mikugami'', and {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}}7 years ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}) from the lower junior fifth rank to the upper junior fifth rank, later {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}}3 years ({{ja There is an article that states that {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} was promoted to the lower rank of Shogoi in 879|Q25001}}.{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Suruga Province|ckb|پارێزگای سروگا|cs|Provincie Suruga|de|Provinz Suruga|eo|Provinco Suruga|es|Provincia de Suruga|fa|ولایت سوروگا|fr|Province de Suruga|gl|Provincia de Suruga|hak|Suruga-koet|id|Provinsi Suruga|it|Suruga (provincia)|ja|駿河国|ko|스루가국|lt|Surugos žemė|nl|Suruga (provincie)|pt|Província de Suruga|ru|Суруга (провинция)|simple|Suruga Province|sk|Suruga (provincia)|sr|Провинција Суруга|th|แคว้นซูรูงะ|tr|Suruga (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Суруґа|vi|Tỉnh Suruga|zh|駿河國|zh_min_nan|Suruga-kok|zh_yue|駿河國|qid=Q864170}} It is described as ``Miho Shrine'' in Rubara County ({{ill|Ihara District, Shizuoka|fa|ناحیه ایهارا، شیزوئوکا|ja|庵原郡|ko|이하라군|nl|Ihara (district)|zh|庵原郡|qid=Q988501}}) and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.In ``{{ill|Suruga no Kuni Fudoki|Q11668491|qid=Q11668491}}'', it is written that ``Japanese Bushihohoku Kansei, Shikken Keida Gohyakuune, Tamekuni no Sangu Shrine.'' Therefore, our company is {{jalink|Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha Shrine|Q653180} in Suruga Province. } ({{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}), it is presumed to have held the position of the third shrine after {{ill|Toyozumi Shrine|Q18337536|qid=Q18337536}} (Ninomiya) {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=151-152}}. However, the basis for writing this in the same article is not clear {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=151-152}}.Among the historical materials of the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, there is a crocodile mouth in the collection of Iimurono Shrine, dated 3 years ({{ill|1319|Q5767|qid=Q5767}}) {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. At this crocodile entrance, it looks like ``Miho Daimyojin,'' and it is said that it was dedicated by the priest's son and wife {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. In addition, in {{ill|Ōan|Q1146245|qid=Q1146245}}3 ({{ill|1370|Q6217|qid=Q6217}}), Date Keimune was ordered to prohibit the felling of sacred trees and search for violators, and {{ill|Kōji (Muromachi period)|Q1143910|qid=Q1143910|lt=Koji}} In the 3rd year ({{ill|1557|Q6595|qid=Q6595}}), {{ill|Yamashina Tokitsugu|Q11470822|qid=Q11470822}} was {{ill|Imagawa Yoshimoto|Q1054305|qid=Q1054305}}, he visited a shrine marked as ``Miura no Daimyojin'' and paid his respects to the Ota clan (Ota clan) of Negi.{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}. In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 5th year ({{ill|1577|Q6704|qid=Q6704}}), Kisaburo Ota was appointed as the chief priest of Miho, and the Daimyojin offering of the shrine, Matsubaraura et al., was relieved.{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.In the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, 106 stones from the three villages of Miho, Orito, and Betsufu were given as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shuinchi}} by {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}}, and the shrine building was was also maintained, but it is said to have been destroyed by fire in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}}8 ({{ill|1668|Q7595|qid=Q7595}}) {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern company rank system}} It was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in 1898|Q7848}}, it was promoted to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.{{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Shiryo|1912}}.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Miho-jinja (Shizuoka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (Shizuoka City designated cultural property)}}]]
The shrine was built by {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}}, but it was destroyed by fire in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}}8 ({{ill|1668|Q7595|qid=Q7595}}) It is said to have been {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Heibonsha)|2000}}, and was later built as a temporary shrine (karimiya) in the middle of the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} and continues to this day<ref name="historical book"/>. The current main shrine is {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} and is designated as a cultural property by Shizuoka City.

From the head of the shrine, a row of pine trees that are about 300 to 400 years old stretches for about 520 meters, called the "path of the gods," until the end of the row of pine trees {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miho no Matsubara}}, {{ill|Yōkyoku|Q8062662|qid=Q8062662}} ``Hagoromo no Matsu'', known for ``Hagoromo'', stands {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}. The pine trees in Hagoromo have been replaced repeatedly due to withering and death, but it is presumed that the original pine trees were an extension of the tree-lined path {{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}.

=== Festival ===
; {{ill|Reisai|Q11385469|qid=Q11385469}}
: {{ill|November 1|Q2997|qid=Q2997}} The most important festival of the year. During the festival, in addition to the ritual of hot water, a shrine maiden dance called ``Hagoromo no Mai'' is dedicated at the Maiden. This hagoromo dance is also dedicated at the autumn festival. <ref name="historical book"/>
; Tsutsugayu festival
: "Tsukayusai". A festival to pray for a good harvest that is held from the night of {{ill|February 14|Q2332|qid=Q2332}} to {{ill|February 15|Q2334|qid=Q2334|lt=15th}}. As part of the ritual, first a large cauldron is set up in front of the shrine and preparations are made to boil porridge. Then, in the middle of the night, a shrine is set up on the beach to welcome the gods, and a ceremony is performed by singing prayers without using any bonfires. The welcomed god resides in a Himorogi, and the Shinto priest carries the Himorogi through a row of pine trees to reach the shrine grounds. Afterwards, porridge is boiled in a large pot in front of the shrine, a bamboo tube is placed in it, and the amount of porridge in the tube is used to predict the year's crop. <ref name="Historic Book"/>{{Sfn|Miho Shrine (Gods)|1987}}

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
* Tachi Mumei (attached to Itomaki Tachi Koshirae) (craft)
*: Written by {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}. The blade is 95.2 cm long and the curve is 4.2 cm <ref name="Yoshisho"/>. Designated on April 30, 1921 (Taisho 10) <ref>{{Nationally Designated Cultural Properties Database|201|6198|Tachi Mumei}}</ref>.

=== Cultural property designated by Shizuoka City ===
*Tangible cultural property
** Main shrine (2 ridge tags, 1 pair of guardian dogs) (building) - Designated on February 23, 1996 <ref name="city designation">{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.shizuoka.jp/000719631.pdf List of city-designated cultural properties]}} (Shizuoka City homepage). </ref>.
** 2 bamboo blinds (craft) - Designated on November 21, 1988 <ref name="city designation"/>.

=== Others ===
* Rip of Feathers
*: A slit that is said to be a piece of hagoromo that appears in the legend of hagoromo <ref name="history book"/>. It is believed to be a piece of Hire/Momo from over 1,200 years ago, and it is also assumed that it originated from the continent based on the pattern of the textile.
* Hagoromo flute - A flute played during the Hagoromo dance.
* Miho old picture map
* Sanhoshaki
